public_rationale: The evidence favors continued human coding: Sonar's October 2025 respondents reported a 42% AI-generated or assisted share, and the 2026 Stack Overflow survey still included developers using no AI tools. These records also show substantial automation. No decisive disappearance event was found. However, Marcus supplied no fixed endpoint for soon, and the referenced prediction contains two horizons. A conclusive supported verdict would require choosing a deadline he did not clearly supply.
limitations: This leaves the forecast open because of its timing, not because the evidence shows human coding disappeared.
Survey responses are self-reported and do not measure all code production.
AI-assisted code can still involve substantial human writing.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Human coding will not disappear soon due to AI.

statement.excerpt: Perhaps I also no longer need to warn people that the idea that coding would disappear soon is bullshit.
statement.document_title: The bad news: AI is going pretty much as I expected

from_speaker: this prediction from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei back in March
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that substantial human code writing will continue in the near term despite AI automation.
Disappearance concerns human code writing across software development, not merely a high AI-generated share at selected companies.
The referenced March forecast provides context, but Marcus does not explicitly adopt either its six-month or twelve-month endpoint.
Soon supplies no latest defensible calendar day. I therefore leave the horizon open rather than silently imposing October 2026 or a one-year deadline.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence that substantial human code writing persists through an endpoint established for soon. Without that endpoint, continued coding supports persistence but cannot conclusively close the forecast.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad evidence that AI has eliminated substantial human code writing within an interval clearly covered by the claim's near-term language.

evidence.locator: Opening discussion quoting Amodei's March prediction
evidence.explanation: The referenced prediction included a twelve-month possibility as well as a three-to-six-month forecast about 90% of code. This explains the context but does not establish which endpoint Marcus committed to.

evidence.locator: Section AI is now a daily habit, not an experiment
evidence.explanation: The reported share is consistent with substantial continuing human coding shortly after Marcus's post. It combines AI assistance with generation and is a survey estimate, not a census of code authorship.
The report dates the observations to October 2025 despite its 2026 title. Its 1,149 respondents were employed or self-employed technology workers who had used AI at work within the preceding year.

evidence.locator: Key findings, AI is used by most developers at work
evidence.explanation: The 2026 survey still describes a substantial developer community, including respondents using no AI tools. It is consistent with persistence, but does not directly measure the worldwide share of code written by humans.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Clarification of the intended endpoint for soon, followed by representative evidence of human code writing through that endpoint. A clearly near-term, independently documented disappearance caused by AI could instead contradict the claim.
